---
title: Walkthrough
---

This walkthrough covers a complete analysis using the bundled **ORD Synthetic** case study — 1,719 census tracts in the Chicago O'Hare metropolitan area with synthetic exposure and mortality data. All values are illustrative; do not use for actual policy decisions.

By the end you will have run a multi-scenario SAF health impact analysis and exported the results.

---

## Step 1 — Launch the dashboard

```bash
python -m bensaf_dash.app
```

Open `http://localhost:8050`. You should see the BenSAF sidebar on the left and the **Data** page in the main panel.

The sidebar **Prerequisites** checklist shows what is needed before the analysis can run. Everything starts unchecked.

---

## Step 2 — Load the example case study

On the **Data** page, find the **Example Case Study** panel on the right side of the page.

1. Open the dropdown and select **ORD Synthetic**.
2. Click **Load Selected Case Study**.

*[Screenshot: Data page after loading ORD Synthetic — success message, prerequisites checklist updating]*

After loading, the sidebar checklist should show tracts, demographics, exposure, and mortality as satisfied. The case study loads:

- **1,719 census tracts** covering Cook, DuPage, Will, Kane, and Lake counties
- **Synthetic UFP exposure** with higher concentrations near O'Hare, decreasing with distance
- **Baseline mortality rates** (0.5–1.2% annual) with realistic county-level variation
- **Population** (~8.6 million total across the study area)

---

## Step 3 — Explore the loaded data

Navigate to the **Explore** page.

Use the variable dropdown to cycle through the loaded inputs:

- **population** — tract-level population counts
- **pollutant_concentration** — baseline UFP (pt/cm³); you should see higher values clustered around ORD
- **mortality_rate** — baseline annual mortality rate per person

*[Screenshot: Explore page — UFP concentration map with O'Hare gradient visible]*

The table below the map shows the first 100 rows of the selected variable. Use this to confirm that GEOIDs look correct and that values are in a plausible range before proceeding.

---

## Step 4 — Configure the analysis

Navigate to **Configuration**.

### Health impact function

The default selection is **Bouma et al. (2023)** — a large-population study linking ambient UFP to natural-cause mortality (HR = 1.012 per 2,723 pt/cm³). Leave this selected.

The dose–response curve on the right shows how relative risk scales with UFP concentration under this function.

*[Screenshot: Configuration page — health function panel with dose-response curve]*

### SAF blend scenarios

The default scenarios are already populated. For this walkthrough, use or add:

- **10%** SAF blend
- **25%** SAF blend
- **50%** SAF blend

Each blend maps to a pollutant reduction via a quadratic polynomial. The plot on the right shows the reduction curve with your scenarios marked.

*[Screenshot: Configuration page — SAF blend scenario list and reduction curve with markers]*

---

## Step 5 — Execute the analysis

In the sidebar, confirm all prerequisites are satisfied, then click **Execute Analysis**.

The analysis runs in a few seconds. The status line will update to confirm completion (or display an error if something went wrong).

*[Screenshot: Sidebar after successful run — all prerequisites green, status line showing completion]*

---

## Step 6 — Review the results

Navigate to the **Results** page.

### Summary cards

At the top, one card per SAF scenario shows:

- **Attributable mortality cases avoided** (mean, lower 95% CI, upper 95% CI)
- **Monetized benefit** (if economic inputs were provided — not in this example)

*[Screenshot: Results page — three summary cards for 10%, 25%, 50% scenarios]*

For the ORD synthetic case study at 50% SAF blend you should expect on the order of tens to low hundreds of cases avoided across the ~8.6M population, depending on the exact synthetic exposure values.

### Scenario comparison chart

The bar chart below the cards compares cases avoided across all three scenarios side by side, with confidence interval bars.

*[Screenshot: Results page — scenario comparison bar chart]*

### Geographic visualization

Select a scenario from the dropdown, then choose a result variable:

- **attributable_cases_mean** — cases avoided per tract
- **delta_concentration** — UFP reduction (pt/cm³) per tract
- **attributable_fraction_mean** — fraction of baseline mortality attributable to UFP

The map updates to show the spatial distribution. Tracts closest to O'Hare should show the largest absolute reductions.

*[Screenshot: Results page — choropleth map showing attributable cases by tract]*

### Detailed results table

Below the map, a tract-level table shows all result columns for the selected scenario. Use this to inspect individual tracts or identify outliers.

---

## Step 7 — Export

Scroll to the **Export** panel at the bottom of the Results page.

- **Summary CSV** — one row per scenario, with total cases avoided and confidence intervals
- **Tract-level CSV** — one row per census tract per scenario, suitable for GIS joins or custom reporting

Download both and open the tract-level file to confirm the structure before using it downstream.
